warningsNotAGuarantee: Warnings come from simple pattern checks. They point at things worth reading, but they can miss harmful content and can flag harmless content.
noWarningsNotAGuarantee: No warnings found. That does not prove it is safe: these are simple pattern checks. Use Preview to read it yourself if you are unsure where it came from.

connector.program: A program that runs on your computer
connector.website: An online service Radium connects to
connector.secrets: Keys and secrets it is given
connector.listToolsRunsProgram: Listing this connector's tools means starting the program above for a moment. The AI cannot use it while you look. Only do this if you trust where it came from.
connector.toolsSelfLabelled: The connector decides which of its tools say they only read. A harmful connector could label a tool wrongly.

permission.markedDangerous: Marked as dangerous by its author
permission.unknownTool: Uses tools Radium does not recognise
permission.runScripts: Run the scripts that come with it
permission.controlPrograms: Start, stop or control other programs
permission.sendWebRequests: Send requests to websites and online services
permission.trashFiles: Move files to the Recycle Bin
permission.browseWeb: Look things up on the internet
permission.instructionsOnly: Only gives the AI written instructions

risk.markedDangerous: Its author says it can do things that are hard to undo.
risk.unknownTool: Radium cannot tell you what these do, so treat them as risky.
risk.runCommands: A command can install or remove software, change settings or delete files. Radium asks before commands it recognises as risky, but not every harmful command is recognised.
risk.runScripts: A script can do anything a command can. Radium asks before each run. Use Preview to read the scripts.
risk.controlPrograms: It could close programs you are using or feed them input.
risk.sendWebRequests: It could send information from your computer to a website.
risk.changeFiles: It could overwrite files you care about. Radium asks before changes outside the chat's folder.
risk.trashFiles: Files go to the Recycle Bin, so they can be restored from there.
risk.changeClipboard: It could replace what you last copied.
risk.showNotifications: It could show notifications that look like they come from somewhere else.
risk.readFiles: It can see the contents of the files it is pointed at.
risk.readGit: It can see your commit history and changes.
risk.seePrograms: It can see which programs are running and what they print.
risk.browseWeb: Pages it reads could contain misleading instructions.
risk.searchDocuments: It can read the documents you have added to Radium.
risk.transcribeMedia: It can listen to the audio and video files it is given.
risk.readClipboard: It can see whatever you last copied, including passwords.
risk.lookAtImages: It can see the images it is given.
risk.instructionsOnly: It cannot act on its own, but its instructions could still steer the AI badly. Use Preview to read them.

warning.downloadAndRun: Downloads something from the internet and runs it straight away
warning.deleteBroadly: Deletes files or folders outside a single project, or a whole drive
warning.readSecrets: Mentions places where passwords, keys or login details are stored
warning.sendData: Sends data from your computer to a website
warning.hideFromUser: Tells the AI to hide what it is doing from you
warning.overrideInstructions: Tries to make the AI ignore its own rules
warning.encodedBlob: Contains a long block of encoded text that cannot be read as it is
warning.unpinnedPackage: Runs a package without a fixed version, so it can change without you knowing
warning.unencrypted: Talks to an address without encryption, so others on the network could read it
warning.shellCommandLine: Hands a whole command line to a shell
